summary: W70 joins the actual readback frame backing, four inline queue entries, active encoder input and tracked PNG allocator requests at synchronized lifetime transitions. The PNG path reads the framebuffer row order directly and shares allocation refusal cleanup with the inventory icon encoder. A controlled worker checkpoint holds the first PNG allocation while three copied slots and four queued frames fill behind its input. At the measured live peak all eight frame backings total 151552 bytes and the encoder requests total 151423 bytes. The pending request checkpoint reaches 303222 bytes. Every admitted frame persists with independently checked orientation; the first receipt checksum matches its PNG. A codec refusal releases all scratch and the same input succeeds on retry. Each native startup run reports capture CPU and GL lifetime evidence. All 46 Release groups, seven related cases and scoped startup checks pass.
